promos.name: PAG-IBIG Announces 2025 Dividend Rates
promos.description: # (BREAKING) PAG-IBIG Announces 2025 Dividend Rates: Regular Savings at 6.62%, MP2 at 7.12% Published: February 27, 2026 | By Chelsea Dione of KKB Research Team KasKasan Buddies was among the organizations invited to attend today’s PAG-IBIG Fund Chairman’s Report 2025, held at PICC Reception Hall in Pasay City. Present also were major media organizations covering the event. We had our team on the ground to bring you the latest updates as they happened. PAG-IBIG Fund has officially announced its 2025 dividend rates at today's Chairman's Report 2025, held at the PICC Reception Hall in Pasay City. If you have PAG-IBIG savings — whether the regular kind or the voluntary MP2 — your money earned for you this year. Here's what you need to know and what to do next. --- # Quick Takeaways • Regular Savings dividend rate for 2025: 6.62% • MP2 Savings dividend rate for 2025: 7.12% • Total dividends declared: ₱64.34 billion — the highest payout in Pag-IBIG’s 45-year history, representing 98.6% of net income (the legal minimum is 70%) • Dividends are credited automatically to your savings account — no action needed on your end • MP2 members may choose to receive dividends as annual cash or let them compound until maturity • Dividend crediting has begun — members can expect to see updated balances in the coming days • Total active PAG-IBIG members: 17.06 million as of 2025 • Total membership savings hit ₱160.41 billion — up 21% from 2024, a new record high • Announced on February 27, 2026 at the PICC Reception Hall, Pasay City --- # The 2025 PAG-IBIG Dividend Rates At the PAG-IBIG Fund Chairman's Report 2025 held today at the PICC Reception Hall, Pasay City, Secretary Jose Ramon P. Ailing, DHSUD Secretary and PAG-IBIG Fund Board Chairperson, officially announced the dividend rates covering calendar year 2025: 2024 and 2023 rates are from previously announced figures. Always verify current rates at pagibigfund.gov.ph. Pag-IBIG Fund Board Chairperson Secretary Jose Ramon P. Ailing's statement: “Pag-IBIG Fund has once again marked 2025 as one of its best-performing years, as we declared the highest amount of dividends in our 45-year history. This past year, we reaffirmed Pag-IBIG Fund's role as the country's leading institution for housing finance and savings. Our strong performance enabled us to deliver higher earnings on members' savings while keeping our housing loans affordable under the Expanded Pambansang Pabahay Para sa Pilipino (Expanded 4PH) Program. We will keep Pag-IBIG Fund's growth sustainable, our programs affordable, and above all, ensure that members receive the benefits they have rightfully earned and truly deserve.” — Secretary Jose Ramon P. Ailing, DHSUD Secretary and PAG-IBIG Fund Board Chairperson Pag-IBIG Fund CEO, Ms. Marilene C. Acosta's statement: “When Pag-IBIG performs well, our members benefit the most. This year's dividend rates of 6.62% for Regular Savings and 7.12% for MP2 Savings reflect our continuing commitment to safeguard members' contributions and ensure they earn strong returns year after year. Our members deserve nothing less than the highest level of public service and the most responsible management of their hard-earned savings. We will begin crediting dividends on the Pag-IBIG Regular Savings and returns on MP2 Savings to members' accounts, and members can expect to see these reflected in the coming days. We encourage our members to create their Virtual Pag-IBIG accounts to conveniently view their updated balances.” — Ms. Marilene C. Acosta, PAG-IBIG Fund Chief Executive Officer --- # PAG-IBIG in 2025: By the Numbers The dividend rates are a direct result of how PAG-IBIG performed in 2025. Here's a quick look at the numbers: Financial Performance • PAG-IBIG's net income for 2025: ₱65.28 billion • Total assets as of end of 2025: ₱1.23 trillion — a new all-time high • Total dividends declared: ₱64.34 billion — equivalent to 98.6% of net income, well above the 70% required by law • This is the highest dividend payout in PAG-IBIG's 45 Membership • Total active members surpassed 17.06 million • Total membership savings reached ₱160.41 billion — a record high, up 21% from 2024 • MP2 savings alone hit ₱83.51 billion, up 31% from 2024 • Voluntary savings (contributions beyond the required ₱200/month minimum) reached ₱93.60 billion — a sign that more members are choosing to save more than required Housing & Loans • Housing loans released: ₱140.54 billion, financing 90,727 housing units • Combined housing and cash loan releases hit ₱199.88 billion — a record high, up 14% from 2024 • Short-term (cash) loans released: ₱94.16 billion — a record high, up 34% from 2024 • Total approved cash loan applications: 3,752,364 — also a record high • Performing loans ratio: 93.58% Digital • The Virtual Pag-IBIG mobile app now has 13.81 million downloads The growth in voluntary savings is particularly worth noting. It suggests that members aren't just parking the mandatory ₱200, they're actively choosing to save more. That collective behavior directly contributes to the fund's strong performance and, in turn, the dividend rates members receive. --- # What This Means for PAG-IBIG Members For Regular Savings members: Your monthly PAG-IBIG contributions earned 6.62% for 2025. PAG-IBIG computes and credits this directly to your savings balance — nothing to do on your end. According to CEO Acosta, crediting has already begun and members can expect to see updated balances in the coming days. Log in to Virtual Pag-IBIG to check. For MP2 members: Your voluntary savings earned 7.12% for 2025. MP2 is designed to earn more than Regular Savings, and that higher rate is intentional. If you opted for annual cash payout, watch for it in your registered disbursement account. If you chose to reinvest, it gets added to your MP2 balance and continues to grow. For those who don't have MP2 yet: At 7.12%, MP2 is worth looking into, especially if you have savings you won't need for the next five years. It is backed by the government, the dividends are tax-free, and there's no market risk involved. Compare it against your current savings or time deposit options and see if it fits your financial goals. --- # How Much Did You Actually Earn? No pressure to open an account either way. Here's a straightforward guide to help you decide. MP2 may be a good fit if you: • Have savings you won't need for at least 5 years • Already have an emergency fund set aside • Want a government-backed, tax-free savings option with no investment risk • Are looking for better returns than a typical bank time deposit Consider building your Regular Savings first if you: • May need to borrow from PAG-IBIG. Your Regular Savings balance supports your cash loan eligibility • Are still working toward a consistent saving routine • Haven't yet reached the contribution requirement for a PAG-IBIG housing loan One important reminder: MP2 has a 5-year lock-in period. Only set aside money you're confident you won't need before it matures. It is a savings program after all, not a substitute for your emergency fund. --- # When Are Dividends Credited And How to Check PAG-IBIG has confirmed that dividend crediting is already underway. Members can expect to see updated balances in the coming days. For Regular Savings members: Your dividend is automatically added to your savings balance. No action required. For MP2 members: • If you chose annual cash payout, it will be sent to your registered bank account or payment channel. • If you chose to reinvest, it gets added directly to your MP2 balance. How to check your balance and dividends: 1. Visit pagibigfund.gov.ph and log in to Virtual Pag-IBIG 2. No account yet? Register using your PAG-IBIG MID number. It's free and straightforward 3. For Regular Savings: go to the "Membership Savings" tab 4. For MP2: go to the "MP2 Savings" tab to view your contributions and dividend history 5. For questions or concerns, reach PAG-IBIG through the hotline or email listed on their official website --- # Frequently Asked Questions Is the MP2 dividend rate guaranteed every year? No. The rate is declared annually based on PAG-IBIG's actual fund performance for that year. It can go up or down. Historically, MP2 has consistently offered a higher rate than Regular Savings, but this is not a guarantee for future years. When will dividends be credited to my account? PAG-IBIG has confirmed that crediting has already begun. Members can expect to see their updated balances in the coming days. Log in to Virtual Pag-IBIG at pagibigfund.gov.ph to check. How do I track my contributions and dividends? Log in to Virtual Pag-IBIG at pagibigfund.gov.ph. Your full contribution history, current savings balance, and dividend credits (for both Regular Savings and MP2) are available in your member dashboard. Can I contribute to MP2 anytime? Yes. MP2 contributions are voluntary and flexible. The minimum is ₱500 per transaction, payable through online banking, GCash, Maya, or over-the-counter at any accredited PAG-IBIG collection partner. There is no required monthly minimum. What happens when my MP2 matures after 5 years? You may withdraw your full savings and all accumulated dividends. You also have the option to renew your MP2 account for another 5-year term. PAG-IBIG will notify you as your maturity date approaches. Are MP2 dividends taxable? No. MP2 dividends are tax-exempt. This is one of the program's key advantages over many other savings products. Do I need an active Regular Savings account to open MP2? Yes. You must be an active PAG-IBIG member with ongoing Regular Savings contributions to open and maintain an MP2 account. What if I missed some contributions — do I still earn dividends? Yes, based on your actual balance. Gaps in contributions simply mean a lower balance, which results in lower dividend earnings. There is no separate penalty for contribution gaps, but saving consistently will always yield more over time. What's the difference between a dividend rate and a bank interest rate? A bank deposit interest rate is fixed and agreed upon before you deposit. PAG-IBIG's dividend rate is declared after the year ends, based on how the fund actually performed, similar to how a cooperative distributes earnings to its members. It is not fixed in advance. I'm an OFW — can I still contribute to MP2? Yes. OFWs may participate through the PAG-IBIG Overseas Filipinos Program and contribute via accredited overseas collection partners or online payment channels. --- # What to Do Next Here's a quick checklist to follow after today's announcement: • Log in to Virtual Pag-IBIG and check your current savings balance • Wait for PAG-IBIG's official crediting advisory, then confirm your dividend was posted • No MP2 account yet? Open one online at pagibigfund.gov.ph — the process is quick and free • Already have MP2? Confirm whether your payout preference is set to cash out or reinvest • Check your MP2 maturity date if you're currently in an active 5-year term • Share this article with someone who has PAG-IBIG savings and might not have heard the news yet --- # A note from PAG-IBIG's leadership At today's event, Secretary Ailing outlined the principles guiding PAG-IBIG's direction going forward: fulfilling every commitment made, completing everything that is started, serving with integrity, and, above all, listening to its stakeholders. For members, that's worth holding them to. LOOK: Whoscall Hosts Community Talk to Strengthen Collaboration Against Scams in the Philippines

In a joint effort to foster stronger collaboration in the fight against scams, Whoscall Philippines hosted its Whoscall Community Talk, gathering key representatives from government agencies, the private sector, educational institutions, and online communities. The event served as a platform to discuss the most pressing scam-related issues affecting different sectors and explore actionable solutions for building a safer digital environment for all Filipinos.

Attendees included members of the Whoscall Philippines team, led by Gogolook Country Head and General Manager Mel Migriño, who presented the “State of Scams in the Philippines.” Other distinguished participants included Ms. Gigi Puno, Chief Information Officer of GoTyme Bank; Atty. Kristina Andal-Escosia from the Department of Migrant Workers Protection Bureau; academic leaders from Asia Pacific College; and student representatives from Mapúa Institute of Electronics Engineers of the Philippines - MU Student Chapter. Online communities such as KasKasan Buddies, FinLit PH, and the Philippine Travel Association also joined to share their experiences and perspectives.

Participants shared firsthand accounts of scam encounters, emphasizing that no one is immune to digital deception. Many stressed the importance of breaking the stigma around discussing scams, noting that open dialogue and shared experiences help raise awareness and prevent future incidents. They called for stronger coordination between government agencies and private organizations to improve collective defenses. Attendees agreed that efforts should shift from being simply reactive to proactive, focusing on education, prevention, and using reliable tools like Whoscall to spot and report potential threats early.

The event concluded with a shared commitment to continued collaboration and advocacy for a more informed, vigilant, and digitally secure Filipino community.

promos.name: Over ₱1 Billion in Discounts Claimed
promos.description: # Your Pag-IBIG Card Just Hit ₱1 Billion in Member Discounts. Here’s How to Make the Most of It The Pag-IBIG Loyalty Card Plus has surpassed ₱1 billion in member discounts across 507 partner establishments. Here’s what it is and how to use it. Published: March 16, 2026 | By Chelsea Dione of KKB Research Team If you are a Pag-IBIG member and you are not using the Loyalty Card Plus, you are missing out on real savings. Pag-IBIG Fund just announced that its Loyalty Card Plus program has given members a total of over ₱1 billion in discounts. That is over a billion pesos saved by Filipino workers on food, medicine, transportation, and other everyday needs. Here is everything you need to know about the card and how to use it. --- # What Is the Pag-IBIG Loyalty Card Plus? Pag-IBIG Fund started the Loyalty Card program in 2014. The idea was simple: give members discounts and special deals at partner stores and businesses. In 2019, they made it better. The new version, called the Loyalty Card Plus, works like a discount card and a basic bank card in one. It is issued through Asia United Bank and UnionBank of the Philippines. You can use it to receive your Pag-IBIG loan money, dividends, and other benefits directly into your account. It also works as a debit card for cashless shopping and gives you access to discounts and rewards at partner stores. It also works as a valid ID for all your Pag-IBIG transactions. So instead of carrying multiple cards, this one card does it all. --- # How Big Has It Gotten? Here are the numbers straight from Pag-IBIG Fund: • Over ₱1 billion in total savings given to members • 507 partner stores and businesses across the Philippines • More than 30 million discount transactions recorded • Over 15 million cards issued to members Those are not small numbers. That is a lot of Filipinos saving money on everyday purchases. --- # Where Can You Use It? The 507 partners cover the things you spend money on regularly. Food, restaurants, and groceries, 114 partners Health and medicine, 189 partners Housing-related stores, 20 partners Fuel and transportation, 5 partners Other stores covering other everyday needs The program is available all over the country: • 162 partners in Metro Manila • 155 partners in the rest of Luzon • 55 partners in the Visayas • 85 partners in Mindanao Wherever you are in the Philippines, there is likely a partner store near you. --- # What the Pag-IBIG Team Said Pag-IBIG Fund Board Chair Secretary Jose Ramon P. Aliling said the program helps members get more value from their money, especially at a time when everything is getting more expensive. Pag-IBIG Fund CEO Marilene C. Acosta shared that a Pag-IBIG Loyalty Card Plus Digital is coming this year. This means you will be able to use your card's benefits on your phone, without needing to carry the physical card around. The goal, she said, is to make the card easier to use for more Filipinos. --- # What Is Coming This Year The Pag-IBIG Loyalty Card Plus Digital is launching sometime in 2026. Once it is out, you will be able to use all the card's features on your phone. The physical card will still be available too. We will update this article as soon as Pag-IBIG Fund shares more details. --- # What This Means for KKBuddies Most of us in this community are working hard to manage our money well. We track our spending, we look for deals, and we try to make every peso count. The Pag-IBIG Loyalty Card Plus fits right into that. If you are already a Pag-IBIG member, you already qualify for this card. That means discounts at grocery stores, pharmacies, and other places you visit regularly. Over time, those savings add up. The card also lets you receive your Pag-IBIG loan money directly, which makes managing your finances a little simpler. Over ₱1 billion in savings tells us that the Filipinos already using this card are making it work. If you have not gotten yours yet, it is worth looking into. --- # How to Get It You can apply for the Pag-IBIG Loyalty Card Plus at any Pag-IBIG Fund branch. Bring a valid ID and your Pag-IBIG membership details. For the full list of partner stores and the latest updates, visit pagibigfund.gov.ph. --- # Stay Updated We will keep you posted on the Pag-IBIG Loyalty Card Plus Digital launch and any new partners added to the program. promos.name: KKB x Fintech Alliance.PH
promos.description: # Fintech Alliance.PH Just Launched a Fraud Intelligence Network. Here’s What It Means for Every Filipino We attended the Fintech Alliance.PH 2026 General Membership Meeting in BGC. Here’s everything announced: from Fraud Intelligence Network launch to blockchain and cybersecurity. Published: March 11, 2026 | By Chelsea Dione of KKB Research Team --- # What Is Fintech Alliance.PH? Fintech Alliance.PH was founded by Lito Villanueva, Executive Vice President and Chief Innovation and Inclusion Officer of RCBC, widely recognized as one of the leading voices in digital finance in the Philippines and across Asia. It has over 140 member companies that together handle more than 95% of all digital financial transactions in the country. Their combined users add up to over 110 million Filipinos. If you use GCash, Maya, a digital bank, or any financial app in the Philippines, you are already part of the world they represent. Every year, they hold a General Membership Meeting where the industry talks about where things are headed. This year, three topics were front and center: protecting Filipinos from fraud, making digital finance safer, and expanding access to financial services across the country. --- # The Big Announcements A New System to Fight Fraud The biggest news of the morning was the official launch of the Fraud Intelligence Data Sharing Network. Here is what it means for you. When one bank or financial app detects a scam, all the other banks and apps in the network are told right away. They all share information with each other so scammers have a much harder time targeting people. For our community, this is a big deal. Scams and fraud are among the top concerns we hear from KKBuddies every day. This is a real step toward making your money safer. --- # Government and Industry Join Forces Against Cybercrime A formal agreement was signed today between the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) and Fintech Alliance.PH. This puts the government and the private sector officially on the same team when it comes to fighting cybercrime and digital fraud. --- # Two More Partnerships Formalized Fintech Alliance.PH also signed agreements with the ASEAN Business Advisory Council and the Rural Bankers Association of the Philippines. The ASEAN partnership is about working together on financial programs across the region. The Rural Bankers partnership is about bringing better digital financial services to communities outside Metro Manila. --- # The Man Behind Fintech Alliance.PH One of the people worth knowing in that room today is Lito Villanueva. He is the founding chairman of Fintech Alliance.PH and the Executive Vice President and Chief Innovation and Inclusion Officer of RCBC. He has spent years working to make digital finance more accessible, more secure, and more inclusive for everyday Filipinos. Under his leadership, RCBC has received over 250 awards for innovation, including recognition as the Best Bank for Digital by Euromoney for five straight years from 2020 to 2024. He has been named among the Top 100 Fintech Leaders in Asia and is widely referred to as "Mr. FinTech of the Philippines." But beyond the titles and awards, what stands out about Villanueva is the work. He has consistently pushed for digital finance that reaches not just people in cities but Filipinos everywhere, including those who have never had a bank account. That mission is exactly what today's General Membership Meeting was about. For our community, he represents what responsible and inclusive digital finance looks like in practice. And it was good to be in the same room. --- # And One More Thing: KasKasan Buddies and Fintech Alliance.PH Are Now Official Partners We also have some personal news to share. Today, we officially signed a partnership agreement with Fintech Alliance.PH. And it made complete sense for us to be there. Our community of 1.3 million KKBuddies are exactly the people that digital finance was built for. We are the everyday Filipinos who use these apps, swipe these cards, and send money through these platforms every single day. We are not just observers of the fintech world. We are part of it. That is why we are here. We want to use our community's reach and voice to help more Filipinos build safe, secure, and responsible money habits. Not just to know more about finance, but to actually feel confident and protected every time they use it. Through this partnership, we will work with Fintech Alliance.PH and its member companies to raise awareness about scams and fraud, promote responsible use of digital financial tools, and help our community make better, safer decisions with their money every day. We are excited about what this means for every KKBuddy. More details coming soon. --- # The Speakers The program was hosted by Rico Hizon, award-winning news anchor with CNBC, BBC News, CNN Philippines, and ANC. Atty. Eugene Teves from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas delivered the keynote. He talked about where the BSP stands on blockchain and digital money, and what rules are being put in place to keep these technologies safe for Filipinos. Joey Concepcion, Chairman of the ASEAN Business Advisory Council, talked about the Philippines' role in the region and what regional cooperation means for everyday Filipinos in terms of access to financial services. Atty. Renato "Aboy" Paraiso, Executive Director of the CICC, talked about the government's push against cybercrime and why everyone, including ordinary Filipinos, plays a role in staying safe online. This session hit close to home for us. Scams come up constantly in our community, and it was good to hear from the people working to stop them. --- # Why This Matters to You Every announcement today connects to something real in your daily life. The new fraud network means the apps and banks you use are now sharing information to protect you better. The agreement with CICC means the government is more formally committed to going after scammers. The push toward rural banks means more Filipinos outside the city will soon have access to the same financial tools that others already enjoy. We will keep you updated as things move forward. # Stay Updated Follow us on social media for updates from today's event and beyond. promos.description: # We Sat Down With the Credit Information Corporation (CIC). Here’s Everything We Learned Our team joined the Credit Information Corporation (CIC) for an R.A. 9510 Orientation. Here’s everything you need to know from that session. Published: March 10, 2026 | By Chelsea Dione of KKB Research Team Another awesome update, KKBuddies! This morning, our team joined the Credit Information Corporation (CIC) for an exclusive R.A. 9510 Orientation: a four-hour deep dive into how the Philippine credit information system actually works. We asked the questions our community has been asking for years, and we got real answers straight from the source. If you've ever been confused about how your credit score is computed, what happens when there's an error on your report, or what your rights are as a borrower, this one's for you. --- # What Is CIC and Why Should You Care? The Credit Information Corporation (CIC) is the government agency behind the Philippine Credit Information System, created under Republic Act 9510. Every time you apply for a credit card or a loan, the lenders involved are required to report your credit data to CIC. That data builds your credit profile, and your credit profile affects whether you get approved, at what rate, and under what terms. Understanding how CIC works is one of the most practical things you can do as a Filipino borrower. Here's everything we learned today. --- # How Your Credit Score Is Actually Computed Your credit score is based on the data that lenders submit to CIC: both the good and the not-so-good. Private companies called Special Accessing Entities (SAEs) are the ones that take that data and compute your actual score. The most important thing you can do to protect your credit profile: pay on time and in the right amount. Everything else builds from there. A few specific things worth knowing: On credit utilization: The 30% rule (keeping your credit card spending at or below 30% of your limit) is a widely recognized benchmark. Lenders ultimately have their own criteria, but staying within that range is a safe habit to build. On BNPL: Using Buy Now, Pay Later services won't significantly hurt your score on its own, as long as you pay on time and in full. It's the payment behavior that matters, not the product itself. On old, unused credit cards: Keeping them open isn't necessarily a problem. What lenders look at most is whether your payment history is clean. --- # How Often Banks Are Required to Report Your Data Banks and financial institutions are required to submit credit data to CIC on or before the 10th of every month. Your credit profile is updated regularly, but there can be a gap between when something happens and when it shows up on your report. If a fully paid loan hasn't reflected yet, this monthly reporting window is likely why. --- # What to Do If There's an Error on Your Report This is one of the most common concerns in our community: errors on credit reports, or loans appearing under your name that you never took out. Here's the exact process CIC laid out: Step 1: Go directly to the lender or financial institution that submitted the data first. Don't file a dispute with CIC right away. The lender may still be in the process of updating their records. Step 2: Only after exhausting all options with the lender (and the error is still showing) should you escalate and file a formal dispute with CIC. One important thing to know about timelines: negative information that has been fully settled stays in the CIC database for up to three years from the date it was resolved. It doesn't disappear the moment you pay it off. Plan accordingly if you're preparing for a major credit application. On submitting entities who fail to submit accurate or updated data: CIC confirmed they can be fined up to ₱30,000 per day for non-compliance. That's a meaningful consequence, and it's good to know it exists. --- # On Fees for Accessing Your Credit Report Accessing your credit report through CIC involves an administrative fee that covers their processing costs. The additional fees you may encounter through accredited bureaus like TransUnion or CIBI come from the specialized tools those bureaus use, and not from CIC directly. --- # A Right Every Filipino Borrower Should Know One point from this morning's session that we think every KKBuddy needs to hear: If a bank or lender rejects your credit card or loan application, they are required to explain why. Refusing to give you a reason is a violation of your rights as a borrower. You are entitled to ask, and they are obligated to answer. If you've ever been rejected with no explanation, you now know you can AND should ask for one. --- # On Fraud and Identity Theft If you suspect someone has used your identity to apply for credit products without your knowledge, act quickly. Contact the lender involved directly and document everything. From there, you can escalate to CIC if needed. CIC shared that they currently have no known instances of a data breach within their system. Accredited institutions connect to CIC through secured, IP-whitelisted channels. That said, staying on top of your credit report regularly is still the best way to catch anything unusual early. --- # On Reaching More Filipinos One part of today's conversation that resonated with us was the discussion around access. CIC acknowledged that many Filipinos, especially those in rural areas and senior citizens, still find it difficult to access credit information digitally. Their plan is to work through LGUs and cooperatives to bring credit education to more communities at the ground level. This is exactly the kind of work we want to be part of. Reaching Filipinos outside Metro Manila, in provinces and key cities, and making financial education genuinely accessible. That's what we're building toward together with CCAP as well. --- # Why We're Sharing All of This We attended this orientation because the more you understand about how your credit data works, the better equipped you are to protect it, build it, and use it to your advantage. That's always been what KKB is about. We'll be breaking down more from today's session in the coming days, including a closer look at the Philippine Credit Information System and what each type of entity actually does. Stay with us, KKBuddies. There's a lot more coming. Wrapping up a great afternoon with Atty. Ben Joshua A. Baltazar, President and CEO of the Credit Information Corporation, and the KasKasan Buddies team. Thank you for having us, CIC! --- # Stay Updated The best financial tips, latest promos, news promos, resources, and everything coming out of this partnership goes straight to our community first. promos.description: # It’s Official: KasKasan Buddies Partners With the Credit Card Association of the Philippines KasKasan Buddies and the Credit Card Association of the Philippines (CCAP) have formally partnered to expand financial education and responsible credit card use across the country Published: March 6, 2026 | By Chelsea Dione of KKB Research Team Big news, KKBuddies! We just made it official with the Credit Card Association of the Philippines (CCAP). We signed a partnership with CCAP today, March 6, 2026, in RCBC, 29th Floor Robinsons Equitable Tower, ADH ave. cor. Poveda, Ortigas, with key people from both our teams in the room, along with a representative from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP). It was a full-circle moment for us, and one we're really glad to finally share with you. --- # Who Is CCAP? CCAP is the official group of credit card companies and banks in the Philippines. Most of the credit cards you use today are issued by CCAP member banks. When it comes to how credit cards work, what protections you have as a cardholder, and how Filipinos are educated about using credit responsibly, CCAP plays a big role in all of that. For us, this partnership means the information we share with our community now has an even stronger foundation behind it. More accurate, more complete, and directly connected to the people who know the credit card industry best. --- # What We're Working On Together So, what does this actually look like in practice? Here's what we and CCAP are actually building together: ✔ Educational videos featuring official CCAP representatives, so you get clear and accurate information straight from people who know what they're talking about. ✔ Meaningful financial literacy sessions every year, open to Filipinos who want to learn more about using credit cards wisely and getting the most out of them. ✔ Improved learning materials, taking what CCAP already has and making it easier for everyday Filipinos to read, understand, and use. ✔ Campaigns on responsible credit card use, spreading the message that a credit card, when used well, can be one of the most helpful financial tools you have. ✔ Community programs and activities that bring our reach together with CCAP's network, all aimed at helping more Filipinos make better money decisions. --- # Who Was There Signing on behalf of CCAP were Chairman Rolando P. Ebreo, President Geraldine C. Liggayu, and Executive Director Alex G. Ilagan. Our CEO and Co-Founder Joel Khristopher Cabugos and Corporate Secretary and Co-Founder Jacques Yves (Jax) Reyes signed on our behalf. Also present from CCAP were Marketing and PR Committee Chairs Gen Rodriguez and Alvin Marana, Vice Chair Tovi De Leon, Secretary Ruth Ramirez, and Marketing and PR Representative Leslie Javier of RCBC. From our team: Chief Marketing Officer Joram Joseph Bonus, Senior Business Development Executive Carl Munsayac, Head of Media Jayvee Mambalo, Digital Content Producer Raphael Lawrence Marabut, and Data Analyst Tricia Daguio. --- # What They Had to Say Joel Khristopher Cabugos, our CEO and Co-Founder: “We’re very honored. This is part of our advocacy and purpose. It just amplifies and validates the campaign and objective of KasKasan Buddies. Moving forward, we’ll be more aggressive in doing financial literacy and financial wellness campaigns — knowing that it’s a big responsibility for a community with this size.” Joel also shared that upcoming programs will prioritize reaching Filipinos outside Metro Manila, covering key cities and provinces, with a special focus on the youth. “That’s something we see will make a lot of impact,” he said. Jax Reyes, our Corporate Secretary and Co-Founder: "This is really about pushing financial literacy — especially the proper use of credit cards and breaking the stigma that credit cards are bad. Because if used correctly, they're genuinely beneficial to a lot of Filipinos." Jax also highlighted the importance of amplifying CCAP's existing programs, which he believes more Filipinos need to know about. "They already have programs that are beneficial to credit card holders in the country," he said. "We want to help more people find out about them." Rolando P. Ebreo, Chairman, CCAP: "Today's signing reflects a shared commitment to expand financial education through relevant, accessible, and engaging platforms. Through this partnership, CCAP and KasKasan Buddies will work together on content, learning sessions, and initiatives that empower more Filipinos to use credit responsibly and confidently." Chairman Ebreo also noted that the collaboration directly supports BSP's push to advance financial inclusion, making sure that knowledge, opportunity, and access reach more communities across the country, not just those in major cities. Geraldine C. Liggayu, President, CCAP: “We’re very thankful that this partnership has finally come true. This has been endorsed not just by CCAP but also by BSP and other schemes like Visa and Mastercard. We’re really looking forward to it! We’re hoping we can educate and reach more Filipinos — not just on responsible credit card use, but on personal finance as a whole. Na hindi sila matakot gumamit ng credit card at maintindihan nila kung paano i-manage ang kanilang personal finances na hindi sila malulubog sa utang. Yun man lang — in that manner, makatulong kami to uplift the lives of the Filipinos.” --- # What This Means for Our Community We started as a Facebook group where Filipinos could share tips on getting more out of their credit cards. Today, we're 1.2 million members strong. Partnering with CCAP connects our community directly with the people who set the standards for credit cards and look after cardholders in the Philippines. And with BSP part of this conversation too, what we're working on together feeds into something bigger: a national push to help every Filipino feel more confident about their money. We're genuinely excited about what comes next. More programs, more resources, and more ways for our community to learn together. We'll keep you posted every step of the way. A big day for our team and for every Filipino cardholder. KKB and CCAP officially join forces to bring better financial education to more Filipinos. --- # Stay Updated The best financial tips, latest promos, news promos, resources, and everything coming out of this partnership goes straight to our community first. promos.description:
SEC Holds "InvestEd Tayo sa Financial Literacy at Responsableng Pag-utang" During Investor Protection Week 2025

November 13, 2025 • Makati City

As part of its lineup of activities for Investor Protection Week 2025, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) held the program InvestEd Tayo sa Financial Literacy at Responsableng Pag-utang at the SEC Headquarters in Makati City yesterday, November 13.

The program featured FinLit Talks with SEC Chairperson Francis Lim alongside popular content creator Jax Reyes of KasKasan Buddies, who shared practical insights on personal finance, money management, and credit card hacks.

A Regulatory Panel Engagement Discussion followed, where esteemed resource speakers shared their expertise on responsible borrowing and consumer protection. The panel included:

• Atty. Sheara Lupango-Tamayo, Director of the SEC Financing and Lending Companies Department

• Ms. Rochelle D. Tomas, Director of the BSP Consumer Protection and Market Conduct Office

• Police Major Sonny B. Galicia, Chief of the General Cybercrime Section–Cyber Response Unit, PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group

• Mr. Tony Isidro, President and CEO of FUSE Financing, Inc.

Participants also enjoyed a variety of fun and educational games with exciting prizes, as well as a Financial Literacy Session by financial journalist and the “Financial Beshie ng Bayan,” Ms. Salve Ibañez (SalveSays)

Attendees were invited to join another round of entertaining events and activities.

Registration for these events was available at events.sec.gov.ph

Courtesy: Securities and Exchange Commission Philippines

promos.name: Start Them Young: Financial Literacy is Crucial
promos.description:
We at KasKasan Buddies are so proud of the success of our “Street Smart Masterclass: Money Masters 101” with Street Smart last Saturday (Dec 13, 2025) at The Loft, BGC!

At KasKasan Buddies, we strongly believe in equipping the next generation with essential life skills. That’s why we were thrilled to partner with Street Smart to host the “Street Smart Masterclass: Money Masters 101.” The highly interactive program was successfully held last Saturday, December 13, 2025, at The Loft, BGC, focusing on delivering fun and engaging financial literacy lessons to kids aged 6 and up.

Demystifying Finance for the Youngest Generation

This foundational masterclass is specifically for children to demystify the world of finance. Through hands-on activities and clear explanations, we ensured each young participant learned fundamental concepts essential for their future financial well-being.

Key Modules Covered in Money Masters 101:

The Basics of Saving: We taught the importance of setting aside money and watching it grow.

Different Budgeting Methods: We introduced simple, age-appropriate ways to manage and allocate funds.

The Foundations of Banking: We gave them a look into how banks work, including the difference between savings accounts and checking accounts, and even a basic lesson on how to write a cheque.

All About Credit and Debit Cards: We clearly explained the distinction between the two and how they are used responsibly.

This initiative highlights the critical role of early financial education. By learning these fundamentals at such a young age, we are confident that our participants are better positioned to make sound financial decisions as they grow older.

This is just the beginning! KasKasan Buddies is committed to continuing this mission. We plan to host more impactful programs and initiatives like Money Masters 101 designed to empower our community. Join our community for more updates!

#BPIInTheNews: BPI Wraps Up Cybersecurity Awareness Month with Content Creators and Partners

As we wrap up our Cybersecurity Awareness Month celebration, BPI brought together content creators and partners who can help champion a safer digital landscape.

Together with the bank’s cybersecurity and fraud experts, BPI shared practical tips on how content creators can protect themselves and their communities from phishing, hacking, and other online scams — carrying the battlecry: “Maging listo. Huwag magpaloko.”

“With innovation and with ease comes the fraudsters. How scams happen to ‘steal’ money is through fraud. And that is now in the control of each individual. So, we want all of you here to help us make content that is different, that people will understand,” said BPI Chief Customer and Marketing Officer Cathy Santamaria.

Through this initiative, BPI aims to empower more voices to amplify cybersecurity reminders and help prevent scams — especially as the holiday season approaches, when cases of cybercrimes tend to rise.

Courtesy: BPI Facebook Page
